---
title: Deploying
navTitle: Deploying
description: Run a LakeQL server in production.
---

A LakeQL project is an ordinary Node application, so it deploys like any Node service. A few things are worth getting right for production.

## Build and Generated Files

The generated endpoint files under your source path are part of your source — commit them, and regenerate with [`pull`](/docs/cli/commands/pull) when a table changes. Build the project with its build script before deploying.

## Environment

Provide the connection variables through your platform's environment or secrets manager rather than a committed `.env`. Validate them at startup so a misconfiguration fails fast. See [environment variables](/docs/lakeql/configuration/environment-variables).

## Lifecycle

The application owns the runtime. Wire `runtime.close()` to `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT` so connections drain cleanly on shutdown, as shown in [server setup](/docs/api/server-setup/create-api-server). The server exposes a health check at `/live` (configurable) for readiness and liveness probes.

## Observability

LakeQL logs every execution error server-side and offers an [`onError`](/docs/api/customization/error-handling) hook to forward errors to your telemetry (OpenTelemetry, Sentry, metrics) without coupling the framework to any provider.

## Containers

The project builds into a standard Node container image. Set the environment at runtime, expose the server port (default `4000`), and run the built entry point.
